title: Ethiopian English National Practice Exam 2014 (1 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 1 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText:
DIRECTIONS: Items 97 - 120 are presented in the form of dialogues. Choose the alternative that is the most appropriate to complete the dialogue.

97) Miriam: What sort of films do you like to watch during your free time?

Sara: ___________
options: I sometimes watch science fiction but I love romantic films.
Films are a good pass-time entertainment.
My favourite actress is Muluaiem.
I haven't watched any films for a couple of weeks.
questions.explanation:
The reply should directly answer the question about the types of films Sara likes.

 Option A does this clearly and appropriately.

questions.questionText:
Teacher:_________

Student: Earthquake is one type of natural disaster.
options: Where do natural disasters occur?
What do you meant by natural disaster?
Give an example of a natural disaster.
When natural disasters occur in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation:
The student's reply provides an example, so the teacher's question must ask for one.

 Option C matches the dialogue appropriately

questions.questionText:
Tariku:____________

Barnabas: I think that is what we need in order to get rid of poverty.
options: There are a lot of challenges that our country is facing.
We must prevent conflicts and live together peaceful.
I do not understand why some people like to cause trouble toothers.
Many young people are in need of jobs.
questions.explanation:
Barnabas' reply refers to addressing poverty, which aligns with providing jobs.

 Option D fits the dialogue context best.

questions.questionText:
Seifu: Surely, the internet is not a perfect invention.

Biruk: What do you mean?

Seifu:___________
options: To put it another way, it has many shortcomings.
Using the internet speeds up our work.
If you want, I can show how use it.
The internet is the art of the technology.
questions.explanation:
Biruk asked for clarification. 
Option A directly explains what Seifu meant, making it the appropriate response.

questions.questionText:
Father: Please let me know that you have arrived there safely.

Daughter:____________
options: I will call you as soon as I reach there.
I'm sure I will be there by this time tomorrow.
I'm sure I will enjoy my flight.
It is going to be a long journey.
questions.explanation: The daughter's reply should directly respond to the father's request to inform him upon arrival. Option A appropriately confirms this.

questions.questionText:
Daughter: Are you ready, Mum?

Mother:___________
options: Yes, we will ready too buy a lot of things.
No, there is no one else coming.
Yes, I am coming.
What are you doing there?
questions.explanation:
The mother’s reply should confirm that she is ready. 

Option C is the appropriate and natural response to the question.

questions.questionText:
Gadissa: I'm very much in need of money but I don't know who I can ask.

Gemechu:_________
options: I asked my elder brother to give some money but he refused.
Why do you need the money?
Our father might give you some if you ask him.
I think we need to save some of the money that we earn every month.
questions.explanation:
Gemechu's reply should suggest a solution to Gadissa's problem. 
Option C offers a helpful suggestion, making it the most appropriate response.

questions.questionText:
Journalist: Do you think there is enough fish for you to catch every day in this lake?

Fisherman:____________
options: The lake is home to different kinds of fish and other aquatic animals.
My livelihood depends on fishing, and I love fishing more than anything else.
Most of us who live around here do fishing both for food and sport.
There are more fishermen nowadays and there aren't enough for everyone.
questions.explanation:
The journalist asked about the availability of fish. 
Option D directly answers this question by addressing the issue of fish scarcity due to many fishermen.

questions.questionText:
Aman: Talking on the mobile phone is not free from problems.

Abdul: How?

Aman:__________
options: There may be sudden connection problem.
Smart phones are expensive for many people.
Everybody has a mobile phone these days.
I don't pick up the phone if I don't want to.
questions.explanation:
Abdul asked for clarification ('How?').
 Option A explains a problem with mobile phones, directly addressing the question

questions.questionText:
Dinku: Traffic accidents continue to be real problems in this city.

Fikru:__________
options: The new roads that are being built in different parts of the city are very wide.
Many people use buses because they are cheaper.
The population of the city is growing fast and the city is expanding in all directions.
Both drivers and pedestrians must be much more careful on the road.
questions.explanation:
Fikru’s response should address the problem of traffic accidents.

 Option D gives advice on how to prevent accidents, making it the most appropriate reply.

questions.questionText:
Farmer 1: Why are we not able to get enough crops from the land recently?

Farmer 2: It is because we have been farming the land for years without making any changes on it.
Farmer 3:_________
options: We should continue to work as hard as we used to.
We always work very hard but we do not produce enough.
We may not even feed our families.
Plus the fact that we have never used fertilizers is another cause.
questions.explanation:
Farmer 3 should add another reason for poor crop yield.

 Option D complements Farmer 2’s explanation by mentioning the lack of fertilizer.

questions.questionText:
Mubarak:__________

Semir: In my case, there were more primary school teachers than in the secondary school.
options: The teachers in my primary school were more helpful than those in my secondary school.
The number of teachers in my secondary school was greater than those in my primary school.
There are many differences between primary and secondary school teachers.
There were many more female teachers than male teachers in my primary school.
questions.explanation:
Semir’s reply points out a general comparison between primary and secondary school teachers. 

Option C introduces this idea, making it the most appropriate opening for the dialogue.

questions.questionText:
Father: _____________

Son: But Dad, I have agreed to study with my friends on Saturday.
options: The weekend is approaching, and you must be looking forward to it.
What are you going to do next Saturday?
You know that your grandmother loves you very much and talks about you always.
I have decided that you will go and visit your grandmother on Saturday.
questions.explanation:
The son's reply shows disagreement with a decision already made by the father.

 Option D appropriately sets up this dialogue.

questions.questionText:
Fikirte: ___________

Hilina: I am your friend and I am always ready to do anything that makes you happy.
options: If you like me, you will go to my parent's house with me tomorrow.
Is there anything I can do for you?
I have some good news to share with you, but don't be in a hurry.
Can you guess what I want to do for you?
questions.explanation:
Hilina’s reply indicates willingness to help, which directly answers Fikirte’s offer to ask for help.
 Option B fits the dialogue appropriately.

questions.questionText:
Garoma: _______________

Alambo: I am against all kinds of discrimination.
options: People with disability could be moderate.
Disability should not be a reason for discrimination.
There are people with disability all over the world.
When did you first hear about discrimination.
questions.explanation:
Alambo’s reply opposes discrimination, so Garoma’s statement must address a reason for discrimination.

 Option B fits the context correctly.

questions.questionText:
Chairperson: Let us discuss how inflation in our country is affecting our work

Participant:___________
options: There is inflation all over the world and there is need for global solution to control it.
I think inflation is difficult to control.
Excuse me for interrupting but we should first discuss the problems in our organization.
There is no doubt that inflation affects the lives of your citizens in many ways.
questions.explanation: The participant expands on the discussion by placing inflation in a global context and suggesting a need for broader solutions, making Option 1 appropriate.

questions.questionText:
Fekadu: Which radio station do you listen to?

Alemu:___________
options: I didn't listen to any radio programmes these last two days.
These days there are many radio programmes to listen to.
Radio Fana programmes are my favourite.
I am not sure how many radio programmes there are at present.
questions.explanation:
The question asks about the radio station Alemu listens to.

 Option C directly answers the question by naming his preferred station.

questions.questionText:
Tesfu: I think we are going to face serious social problems in our city.

Bereket: How?

Tesfu:___________
options: All of us have a responsibility to tackle our social problems.
To give you an idea, there are too many unemployed young people in the city.
The solution to our problems is for us sit together and work towards a common goals.
The administration is doing its best to create jobs to reduce the number of unemployed people.
questions.explanation:
Bereket asked for clarification ('How?'), so Tesfu should give a specific example of the social problem.
 Option B explains the issue directly.

questions.questionText:
Ahmed: I was very hungry and actually ate a lot at lunch time.

Muhaba:___________
options: They say hunger is the best sauce.
Food has become expensive recently.
I and my best friend eat lunch frequently.
I usually can't find a good place to eat.
questions.explanation:
Muhaba’s response should be a comment on Ahmed’s statement about eating a lot due to hunger. 
Option A is an appropriate proverb that relates directly to the situation.

questions.questionText:
Foreigner: _________

Welde: Oh, sorry, I don't know. I don't live in this part of the city.
options: Can you tell me where the Capital Hotel is?
Excuse me. Do you live near here, if I may ask?
Can I talk to you for a minute, please?
How long have you been living here?
questions.explanation: Welde’s reply indicates he does not know a location. Option A is the only question that asks for directions, making it the appropriate opening.

questions.questionText:
The Chairman: People who live in this Wereda face a lot of problems

Participant:___________
options: The awful thing is nobody seems to be concerned about solving any of their problems.
The population of this Wereda are hardworking.
I feel that it is not the best way of problem solving like this in the future, Mr. Chairman.
The people of this Wereda have respect for one another.
questions.explanation:
The participant’s reply should continue the discussion about the problems.

 Option A comments directly on the lack of action regarding these problems, making it the most appropriate response.

questions.questionText:
Student: I am sorry but I haven't understood your last point.

Teacher:________
options: I don't think you understand.
You will have some point about it.
Do you have any other questions?
Ok. Let me rephrase what I just said.
questions.explanation: The student asked for clarification. Option D appropriately responds by offering to explain the point again in simpler terms.

questions.questionText:
Temesgen: Modern health treatment has become far too expensive these days.

Dilamo:_________
options: There are more medical doctors nowadays.
I have no option but go to a traditional healer because the treatment is less expensive.
If you cannot afford to pay you better stay at home.
We need to get treatments when we become ill.
questions.explanation:
Dilamo’s reply should relate to the high cost of modern treatment.
 Option B directly addresses the problem by offering an alternative solution.

questions.questionText:
Duressa: Are you the eldest in your family?

Demitu:_________
options: My sister is older than me.
My brothers are all older than me.
I am the youngest of the children of my family.
We are a large family with four children.
questions.explanation: Duressa asked if Demitu is the eldest. Option C directly answers this question by stating her position in the family.

questions.questionText:
Manager: What do you think of buying a new vehicle for our office? 

Deputy: _________ , we are short of budget. Besides, there is no need for one.
options: What I think is
I really feel
If you ask me
To begin with
questions.explanation: 'If you ask me' is used to give an opinion, which fits the deputy's response explaining why buying a new vehicle is unnecessary.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is least relevant to a paragraph whose topic sentence is 'Public transportation can reduce urban traffic congestion'?
options: Buses can carry many passengers at once.
Reliable bus routes may reduce the number of private cars on the road.
Efficient public transportation can encourage commuters to leave their cars at home.
Many professional football matches attract thousands of spectators.
questions.explanation: The football sentence does not support the paragraph's central idea, so it breaks relevance and unity.

questions.questionText: She plans ___ her studies next year.
options: continuing
continue
to continue
continued
questions.explanation: Plan is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: Tensions between the two countries are rising quickly. We cannot **rule out** the possibility that war breaks out.
options: assume
exclude
predict
imagine
questions.explanation: To **rule out** a possibility means to dismiss it, exclude it, or determine that it is impossible or irrelevant. Therefore, **exclude** is the closest synonym to the phrase 'rule out' in this context.

questions.questionText: I didn't do it intentionally but I know she got very angry ____________ me. I will apologize to her anyway.
options: upon
with
by
at
questions.explanation:
The correct preposition to use with the verb phrase 'to be/get angry' when referring to a person is 'with'.

 The structure is 'angry with (a person)' or 'angry at (a person/thing)'. 'Angry with me' is the standard and most idiomatic usage.

questions.questionText:
Complete the dialogue:
Parent: You are right; wearing a uniform should be compulsory for class attendance.
Teacher: . . .
options: It isn't very disappointing to see students in the classroom without their uniform
Is it very disappointing to see students in the classroom without their uniform
When do we see students in the classroom without their uniform
Why do we see students in the classroom without their uniform
questions.explanation: The Parent states an opinion agreeing with the compulsory uniform policy ('You are right...'). The Teacher's response should logically relate to why the policy is necessary. Option B, **'Is it very disappointing to see students in the classroom without their uniform'**, is the only response phrased as an interrogative that flows logically as a rhetorical question following the parent's agreement. The teacher is seeking confirmation or shared feeling about the negative state of students not wearing a uniform.

questions.questionText: Choose the best reduced form of: "After he finished his work, he went home."
options: Having finished his work, he went home.
Finished his work, he went home.
Having finish his work, he went home.
Finishing had his work, he went home.
questions.explanation: "Having finished" shows that finishing occurred before going home.

questions.questionText: The committee has ___ money remaining, but it is enough to finish the project.
options: little
little
few
several
questions.explanation: A little indicates a small amount that is nevertheless available.

questions.questionText: __________ a chance to visit any historical site in Ethiopia?
options: Had/have
Did/have
Have/had
Have/have
questions.explanation: The question is asking about an experience that occurred at some point up to the present, requiring the **Present Perfect tense**: **Have you ever had** a chance... The structure is: **Have** (auxiliary verb for Present Perfect) + **you** (subject) + **ever** + **had** (past participle of 'to have'). Therefore, **Have/had** is the correct pair.

questions.questionText: My mobile phone is missing. I ________ dropped it somewhere.
options: would have
might have
couldn't have
haven't dropped
questions.explanation:
The first statement establishes a present problem ('missing phone').

 The second sentence offers a possible explanation for a past action. 

The modal verb 'might have' is used to express a possibility in the past (it is possible that I dropped it). 'Couldn't have' expresses impossibility, which contradicts the fact that the phone is missing.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The children were frightening by the story.
The children were frightened by the story.
The children were frighten by the story.
The children were frightening the story.
questions.explanation: The children experience fear, so frightened is correct.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a possible cause of undue stress?
options: Loneliness and isolated life
Failure to afford a living
Having a wife who is not interested in
Disagreement between spouses
questions.explanation:
The previous passage (Reading Passage I, Paragraph 4) lists causes of stress as: 'Poor marital relationships' (Disagreement between spouses/Having a wife who is not interested in), and 'unemployment' (Failure to afford a living).

 The phrase 'Sometimes getting notified life' (Option A) is unclear and does not align with any of the specific, straining life situations listed in the reading passage as a cause of undue stress, making it the correct 'NOT' cause.

questions.questionText: Professionals specializing in History and Heritage Management have tried their level best to ____________ unique features of notable historical places by undertaking large scale research works.
options: visit
explore
travel
joke
questions.explanation:
'Explore' means to investigate, study, or examine something carefully in order to discover information about it.

 Since the professionals are conducting large-scale research on historical places, 'explore' is the most appropriate verb.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a subject line in a formal letter?
options: To introduce the theme of the letter
To present the details of the letter
To show the receiver's name
To conclude the letter
questions.explanation: The subject line provides a brief summary to state the main topic or purpose (theme) of the letter.

questions.questionText: It appears the **combined effort** by the team significantly contributed to the victory. In fact, we need to take a lesson and reshape our strategy.
options: disarray
power
synergy
dismay
questions.explanation:
The phrase combined effort refers to the cooperative interaction of elements that produces a total effect that is greater than the sum of the individual effects.

 Synergy (Option C) is the exact term for this concept, making it the best substitute.

questions.questionText:
Complete the dialogue:
Khalist: . . .
Hana: With sugar, please.
options: Would you prefer your coffee with or without sugar
How much sugar do you like in your coffee
Is it good to drink coffee without sugar
Do you like your coffee with sugar
questions.explanation: Khalist's question must present a choice that leads to the answer **'With sugar, please.'** Option A, **'Would you prefer your coffee with or without sugar'**, is a direct and standard question offering the two choices presented in Hana's reply.

questions.questionText: Children _____________ abide by the cultural norm of the society.
options: would not
can
might
should
questions.explanation: 'Should' is used to express duty, obligation, or social expectation regarding societal norms.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an ellipsis to show hesitation?
options: I... I don't know what to say.
I; I don't know what to say.
I: I don't know what to say.
I, I don't know what to say.
questions.explanation: An ellipsis can indicate hesitation or an unfinished thought.

questions.questionText: They believe that the documents were destroyed deliberately.
options: The documents are believed to destroy deliberately.
The documents are believed to have been destroyed deliberately.
The documents believed to have destroyed deliberately.
The documents were believed destroying deliberately.
questions.explanation: A completed passive event after believe takes to have been + V3.

questions.questionText:
Arkato: High school students should get training on note-taking skills.

Hagos: ____________________. Not now; they can have it when they join university.
options: This could save their study time
I think you are right
I don't agree with you
Sure; I agree with you
questions.explanation: Hagos disagrees with doing it now and suggests delaying it until university ('Not now...'), making 'I don't agree with you' the logical choice.

questions.questionText: In the coming months, contemporary artists will hold _____________ exhibition of their works.
options: few
the
an
a
questions.explanation: 'An' is the correct indefinite article before the singular countable noun 'exhibition', which begins with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly punctuates the direct quotation?
options: The teacher said "You must revise this chapter."
The teacher said, "You must revise this chapter."
The teacher said; "You must revise this chapter."
The teacher said: "You must revise this chapter."
questions.explanation: A comma commonly separates a reporting clause from a following direct quotation.

questions.questionText: He finally finished ___ the research report.
options: write
writing
to write
wrote
questions.explanation: Finish is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: Don't risk ___ your entire investment.
options: lose
to lose
losing
lost
questions.explanation: Risk is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: 80. Choose the word that is correctly spelt.
options: Asuage
Hospitalty
Asumption
Consumable
questions.explanation:
'Consumable' is correctly spelled.

 The correct spellings for the others are: Assuage, Hospitality, and Assumption.

questions.questionText: Emperor Haile Selassie ___________ from 1930 to 1974.
options: subjugated
dominated
powered
reigned
questions.explanation: 'Reigned' means to rule as a monarch (king or emperor) during a specific period of time.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "The ___ students listened carefully to the professor."
options: interesting
interested
interest
interests
questions.explanation: The students experience interest, so interested is correct.

questions.questionText: The company has to replace all defective products.
options: All defective products have to be replaced.
All defective products have to replaced.
All defective products are having to be replaced.
All defective products had to be replaced.
questions.explanation: Have to passive is have/has to be + V3; products requires have.

questions.questionText:
The Promise and Threat of Artificial Intelligence

1  Artificial Intelligence (AI) is no longer a futuristic dream – it is embedded in nearly every aspect of modern life. From voice assistants and medical diagnostics to autonomous vehicles and personalized education, AI has transformed the way we live and work. Yet, alongside these innovations come ethical concerns and existential questions. As machines become smarter, society must grapple with issues of control, bias, and responsibility.

2  AI's potential to improve human life is enormous. In healthcare, machine-learning algorithms can analyze medical images with remarkable precision, sometimes surpassing human doctors in detecting diseases. In education, AI-driven tutoring systems adapt to each student's learning pace, making instruction more individualized than ever. Businesses use AI to predict market trends, optimize logistics and improve customer experience. These advancements promise greater efficiency and accuracy, saving time, money, and even lives.

3  However, the darker side of AI is becoming increasingly visible. Algorithms trained on biased data can reinforce discrimination. For example, the use of AI in law enforcement or credit scoring may unfairly target minorities. Another fear is the displacement of workers. As automation expands, millions may lose jobs to machines, especially in manufacturing, transportation, and customer service. Moreover, the greatest concern lies not in lost employment but in the potential loss of human agency. If machines begin to make moral or strategic decisions independently, who is accountable for their actions? This question becomes urgent in fields such as autonomous weapons or judicial decision-making. Should a self-driving car decide whom to save in an unavoidable crash? Should AI recommend a prison sentence? These moral dilemmas have no easy answers.

4  Scientists like the late Stephen Hawking and entrepreneur Elon Musk have warned that uncontrolled AI development could pose existential risks to humanity. If an AI system were to surpass human intelligence and act on goals misaligned with human values, it could become uncontrollable. This scenario, though still theoretical, raises the need for global cooperation and ethical frameworks to ensure that AI development remains safe and beneficial.

5  Nevertheless, pessimism is not the only response. Many experts argue that with proper regulation, transparency and oversight, AI can serve as humanity's greatest tool. Organizations are already establishing guidelines for "ethical AI," emphasizing fairness, accountability and respect for privacy. Researchers are also designing systems that can explain their reasoning , reducing the 'black box' problem that makes AI decisions opaque 

6  Ultimately, the future of AI will depend on human wisdom rather than machine intelligence. Technology itself is neutral – it mirrors the intentions of those who design and use it. If society invests as much in ethics and education as it does in innovation, AI could not become a threat, but it is reasonably considered as an ally in solving humanity's most urgent problems – from climate change to disease eradication. The challenge lies in ensuring that intelligence, whether artificial or human, serves the common good.

Which one of the following is NOT true according to paragraph 3?
options: AI can reinforce discrimination if it is filled with biased information.
AI can reasonably create job opportunities for new applicants.
AI may unfairly target individuals who need justice.
AI may expose the potential loss of human agency.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 states that millions may lose jobs due to automation, not that AI creates job opportunities.

questions.questionText: If I had seen the movie, I ______ you about the ending now.
options: would tell
would have told
would be telling
will tell
questions.explanation: This is a Mixed Conditional: Past condition ('If I had seen...') with a present result ('would be telling you now').

questions.questionText: Obviously, the car is very expensive, ___________ it is fuel-economical. If I had the money, I'd go for it.
options: but unlike that
even so
but on the other hand
in addition
questions.explanation: 'But on the other hand' correctly contrasts two different aspects of the car: it is expensive, but it is fuel-economical.

questions.questionText: The committee has ___ money remaining, so the project will probably be cancelled.
options: little
few
little
several
questions.explanation: Little emphasizes an insufficient amount.

questions.questionText: The researcher ___ an old journal article that directly supported her hypothesis.
options: came across
came back
came in
came out
questions.explanation: "Come across" means to find something unexpectedly.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly asks about past external obligation?
options: Did you have to work yesterday?
Did you had to work yesterday?
Did you must work yesterday?
Had you have to work yesterday?
questions.explanation: Did + subject + have to correctly forms the question.

questions.questionText:
Africa could be labeled the supplier of mostly unprocessed products to the rest of the world. The crystal fear that the continent is left behind in its development efforts to provide the same for the rest of the globe. One cannot deny that Africa still has untapped natural resources and human resources even after the long and bloody experience of slaves and colonialism. It is arguable whether or not Africa can be characterized as a high continental trade integration. Such a move, according to many commentators, is believed to help the continent to take the place it deserves.

2

Needless to say, continents apart from Africa, especially those in the northern hemisphere, have developed a special type of system that unites one another and fosters their development in every aspect. These could not have achieved what the rest of the continents have accomplished. It is undeniable that Africa has sacrificed its opportunities for the sake of the rest to prosper uninterruptedly. It was a good clear way to rectify the course of the system. African nations have designed special strategies to achieve their vision to create Africa we want through the Agenda 2030 and Agenda 2063 of the African Union. In this long-term agenda, African nations, through their leaders have signed multiple agreements to meet the desired goals.

3

Some of the notable measures that followed those multiple agreements are the points of focus of this paragraph. In this respect, continental Africa has taken tangible actions to circumvent the challenges arising from the stereotyped way of doing trade including the adoption of an action plan for the implementation of the continental trade. The trade agreement, when operationalized, will liberalize trade in goods. It is also expected to liberalize trade in services gradually and open the door for the elimination of 90% of tariffs in goods. It is also expected to liberate trade in services.

4

Moreover, in recent years, regional economic partnerships have been strengthened. Accordingly, the Tripartite Free Trade Area which incorporates EAC, COMESA, and SADC was regionally economic partnership endorsed in June 2015 in Sharm-el-Sheikh, Egypt with the aim of fostering integration and helping member states to circumvent the challenges arising from overlapping memberships. As of July 2022, there were 22 signatories to the Tripartite Free Trade Area Agreement. The 29 states of the three regional communities and 11 states had ratified it. Three additional ratifications are required to operationalize the Tripartite Free Trade Area.

5

To achieve what has been planned and see the Africa we want, every stakeholder group as well as the wider society must work for the intended goals. Organizations such as the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) confirmed that it will provide technical support and other necessary analysis in order to enhance the initiatives mentioned above.

 Which of the following would be the best replacement for the word **chewy** in paragraph 2 of this passage?
options: tough
boring
sickening
in accessible
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: The road signs indicate that the highway is closed. We _____ use that route tonight.
options: must
may
could
can't
questions.explanation: The closure strongly indicates that using the route is impossible or not possible under the circumstances.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT characteristic of the sick building syndrome?
options: It is the result of the combined effect of various diseases.
It commonly occurs in homes with little or no ventilation.
It is an indistinct collection of symptoms.
It is becoming more common in big cities with small but over-furnished houses.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 5 defines sick building syndrome as a vague collection of symptoms caused by poor ventilation, not by various diseases.

 Therefore, 'It is the result of the combined effect of various diseases' is NOT a characteristic.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a passive perfect participle?
options: Having completed the task, she rested.
Having been warned about the danger, they left.
Being warned about the danger, they left.
Warning about the danger, they left.
questions.explanation: Having been + V3 forms a passive perfect participle.

questions.questionText:
Section One: Word Order

DIRECTIONS: Items 77- 94 are related to different aspects of writing. Choose the best answer from the alternatives.

1) read/notes/you/to/the/must/your/test/do
options: You must read your notes to do the test.
You must do read the test notes to your.
The test notes to read you must your do.
Read notes must to your do the test you.
questions.explanation: The correct word order for the sentence is: 'You must read your notes to do the test.'

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the Oxford comma?
options: She bought bread, cheese and fruit.
She bought bread, cheese, and fruit.
She bought bread cheese, and fruit.
She bought bread, cheese; and fruit.
questions.explanation: The Oxford comma appears before and in a three-item list.

questions.questionText: The company has decided to ___ a new accounting system next month.
options: bring up
take on
carry out
put up with
questions.explanation: "Take on" can mean to accept or undertake new work or responsibility.

questions.questionText: The engineer is responsible ___ checking the equipment before each experiment.
options: of
for
with
about
questions.explanation: "Responsible for" is the standard combination.

questions.questionText: The witness was abroad during the entire month. He _____ have seen the incident in person.
options: may
might
could
couldn't
questions.explanation: Being abroad during the entire period makes personally seeing the incident impossible or extremely unlikely.

questions.questionText: They could not identify the person in the photograph.
options: The person in the photograph could not be identified.
The person in the photograph could not identified.
The person in the photograph was not could be identified.
The person in the photograph could not have identify.
questions.explanation: Negative modal passive is could not be + V3.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly demonstrates agreement inside a relative clause?
options: The students who studies hard usually succeed.
The student who study hard usually succeeds.
The students who study hard usually succeed.
The student who study hard usually succeed.
questions.explanation: The antecedent 'students' is plural, so the relative-clause verb is 'study'.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the correct participle form after "having"?
options: Having wrote the letter, she left.
Having written the letter, she left.
Having writing the letter, she left.
Having write the letter, she left.
questions.explanation: Having must be followed by the past participle written.

questions.questionText: What does the writer specifically say about America in relation to child abuse?
options: Wealthy Americans are the main actors in child abuse.
Tomorrow's America will have less child abuse.
Americans are intentionally creating another generation of child abusers.
American children abused today and will abuse others when they grow up.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 states that child abuse is 'a national plague that experts say is likely to create another generation of child abusers in America from among those being abused today.' This matches Option D.

questions.questionText: Ethiopia will enjoy a period of peace and __________ in the next few years, this happens if the country ensures law and gives priority to science, technology and innovation.
options: prosperity
nationality
protest
disparity
questions.explanation:
The sentence links peace and a positive outcome with prioritizing science, technology, and innovation.

 The most logical and positive outcome that goes hand-in-hand with peace and development is prosperity, which means being successful in material terms; flourishing economically.

questions.questionText: The company will complete the training program by June.
options: The training program will have completed by June.
The training program will be completed by June.
The training program is completed by June.
The training program was completed by June.
questions.explanation: Future simple passive uses will be completed.

questions.questionText: The professor ____________ I met is from Kenya.
options: which
whose
whom
where
questions.explanation: 'whom' is the relative pronoun used to refer to a person when they are the object of the verb ('I met [him]').

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a semicolon in a contrast between closely related ideas?
options: The first method is inexpensive; the second is more reliable.
The first method is inexpensive, the second is more reliable.
The first method; is inexpensive the second is more reliable.
The first method is inexpensive: the second is more reliable.
questions.explanation: A semicolon appropriately joins two closely related independent clauses.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct connective: He is poor ____ he is honest.
options: but
although
because
so
questions.explanation: Contrast requires 'but'.

questions.questionText: if/they/have/us/phoned/we/joined/them/had/would
options: We have if would them us had they joined phoned.
They would joined them have phoned if had we us.
If phoned them would they joined us have we had.
They would have joined us if had phoned them.
questions.explanation: Correct conditional sentence: 'They would have joined us if they had phoned.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Break the ice'.
options: Start a conversation
Destroy something
Freeze water
Stop talking
questions.explanation: Means to make people feel more comfortable socially.

questions.questionText: _____ the first proposal focuses on cost, the second emphasizes quality.
options: Because
Whereas
Due to
Because of
questions.explanation: Whereas emphasizes the contrast between the two proposals.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'in' rather than 'of'?
options: He is the fastest runner of the school.
He is the fastest runner in the school.
He is faster runner in the school.
He is the most fastest runner in the school.
questions.explanation: In is used with an organization or place such as the school.

questions.questionText: ___ students who attended the seminar received ___ certificate at the end of the session.
options: Ø / a
The / an
The / a
Ø / the
questions.explanation: "Students" is a general plural noun, while "certificate" is a singular countable noun referring to one certificate per student.

questions.questionText: "Are you ready for the interview?" The manager asked me. Choose the correct report.
options: The manager asked me if was I ready for the interview.
The manager asked me whether I was ready for the interview.
The manager asked me whether was I ready for the interview.
The manager told me if I was ready for the interview.
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions use if or whether and statement word order.

questions.questionText: If only she ______ the warning before making the decision.
options: noticed
had noticed
would notice
has noticed
questions.explanation: A past regret requires Past Perfect after if only.

questions.questionText: In which sentence does 'while' express time?
options: While the first method is simple, the second is more reliable.
While the two brothers are similar, their personalities differ.
While she was preparing dinner, the phone rang.
While the old machine is slow, the new one is efficient.
questions.explanation: The clause describes an action occurring during another action.

questions.questionText: In a well-organized formal letter, what should the second main body paragraph generally contain?
options: The sender's address
Important details, facts, or explanations
The signature only
The subject line
questions.explanation: The second paragraph normally develops the important supporting details.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I can solve the problem myself," Lina said?
options: Lina said that she could solve the problem herself.
Lina said that she can solved the problem herself.
Lina told that I could solve the problem myself.
Lina said that she had solved the problem herself.
questions.explanation: Can changes to could; the statement does not say that she actually solved it.

questions.questionText: His parents let him ___ abroad alone.
options: to travel
travel
traveling
traveled
questions.explanation: Let is followed by object + bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: The manager asked the employees to ___ the outdated procedure and replace it with a more efficient one.
options: get rid of
get over
get along with
get back
questions.explanation: "Get rid of" means to remove or eliminate something.

questions.questionText: Which revision would most improve the unity of a paragraph about the benefits of exercise?
options: Add a sentence explaining how exercise improves cardiovascular health.
Add a sentence describing the writer's favorite football team.
Add a sentence about the history of a nearby stadium.
Add a sentence about the price of sports shoes.
questions.explanation: Cardiovascular health directly supports the topic of exercise benefits.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly distinguishes 'easy' and 'easily'?
options: The question was easily, and she answered easy.
The question was easy, and she answered easily.
The question was easy, and she answered easy.
The question was easily, and she answered easily.
questions.explanation: Easy describes the question; easily describes answered.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "spoken"?
options: She has spoke to him.
She has spoken to him.
She is spoken to him.
She had speaking to him.
questions.explanation: Spoken is the V3 form of speak.

questions.questionText: Before submitting the report, the students carefully ___ the statistical calculations to identify any errors.
options: went over
went out
went back
went ahead
questions.explanation: "Go over" means to review or check carefully.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'nevertheless' most appropriately?
options: The service has improved; nevertheless, several problems remain.
The service has improved; nevertheless therefore it is good.
Nevertheless because the service improved.
The service nevertheless because improved.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless appropriately introduces a contrasting point.

questions.questionText: When we were in Gambella, every day after work, we _____________sit by the river watching fishers caught the big fish called 'gur' and made a lot of money out of it.
options: were used to
are used to
have used to
used to
questions.explanation: Used to' expresses a past habit. The sentence describes something that happened regularly in the past when they were in Gambella

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "These are my books," she said?
options: She said that these were my books.
She said that those were her books.
She told that those are her books.
She said that those had been my books.
questions.explanation: These can become those and my becomes her.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the comparative of far?
options: The second village is farther from the city than the first.
The second village is farthest from the city than the first.
The second village is more far from the city than the first.
The second village is farrer from the city than the first.
questions.explanation: Farther is an accepted comparative form of far.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses increasing expense?
options: Life is becoming expensiver and expensiver.
Life is becoming more and more expensive.
Life is becoming most and most expensive.
Life is becoming more expensive and most expensive.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives use more and more.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the punctuation needed to make the intended meaning clear?
options: Let's eat Grandma!
Let's eat, Grandma!
Let's eat; Grandma!
Let's eat: Grandma!
questions.explanation: The comma shows that Grandma is being addressed rather than identified as food.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses a colon incorrectly?
options: She had one objective: to finish the project.
The box contained three items: a pen, a ruler, and a notebook.
My favorite subjects are: English and Biology.
He remembered one important rule: never give up.
questions.explanation: A colon should not normally separate a verb directly from its complement.

questions.questionText: Sara said to me, "We saw them yesterday." Which is correct?
options: Sara told me that we had seen them the day before.
Sara told me that they had seen us yesterday.
Sara said me that we saw them the previous day.
Sara told me that we have seen them tomorrow.
questions.explanation: We remains we from Sara's perspective, past simple becomes past perfect, and yesterday becomes the day before.
